article.name: Context Infrastructure
article.summary: Context Infrastructure is a Markdown-based workspace blueprint for coding-agent rules, dated observations, and scheduled L1/L2 agent jobs. Its observer appends tagged observations and its current reflector proposes rule changes for human approval before apply. The review is pinned to the verified main head; no runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run.

who_what.text: The official README presents Context Infrastructure as a reference implementation and workspace blueprint for AI coding agents, with rules, skills, observations, and scheduled jobs; it is not a configured hosted service.
The official repository page identifies main as the default branch. Its main commit feed reports full head 74511fbd5465ac302524d9e6878fab85727fc645, updated 2026-11-24T18:54:32Z.

architecture.text: The documented memory structure has session-start L3 rules, a dated L1 observation log, and L2 reflection. Canonical records are Markdown files in the workspace; the trigger scripts delegate inspection and synthesis to an OpenCode agent.

L1 entries use date headers and High/Medium/Low tags; the PRD describes pulling only task-relevant observations. Semantic search was moved to a separately installed skill repository and is not implemented by this repository alone.
The observer and reflector configure workspace paths in script constants and create OpenCode sessions through a local client; there is no central database or service described for this core.

behavior.text: Write: the L1 observer checks for an existing date entry, scans workspace changes through an OpenCode agent, and prompts it to append tagged observations and include root-relative file paths. The agent, rather than the trigger script, performs content filtering and summarization.

Update/correction: same-date observer runs skip instead of revising an existing entry. The current reflector's default mode writes rule candidates containing target, change, rationale, and source observations; a rules-directory hash snapshot detects rule edits during proposal generation. A human must approve candidate checkboxes before a separate --apply invocation changes rules.

Delete/retention: approved apply merges selected candidates, archives them in the candidate file, and garbage-collects observations; the prompt also removes expired Low entries. The inspected Markdown workflow does not establish erasure from Git history, backups, or copies.

Retrieval: AGENTS.md routes the session into rules and workspace instructions; the PRD describes agent-driven pull of sparse relevant observations. Semantic search is external/optional, and no ranking API or answerability gate was established in this repository review.

Scope isolation: the model is one workspace's shared rules and observation log. The inspected scripts and design do not provide user/tenant/project authorization; deployment must isolate workspaces and enforce filesystem/runtime permissions.

Provenance: observation entries are dated and tagged, and prompts request relative file paths. Reflector candidates identify source entries, rationale, and intended rule edits. The inspected workflow does not establish durable claim-level citations, truth states, or mutation history; priority tags are not truth verification.

Efficiency/observability: plain-text append and selective reads avoid a required database; jobs delegate work to OpenCode. The reflector hashes rules before and after proposal generation. Runtime depends on cron, configured local paths, a working OpenCode server, and model execution; no quantitative performance/usage telemetry was established.

metrics.evidence: No adjudicated query workload or answerability gate was run or established in inspected core sources.
Human-approved rule changes exist, but no correction or stale-retrieval probes were run.
Apply-stage observation garbage collection is implemented; no post-delete checks across history, backups, or copies were run.
Workspace-based scope is visible, but no cross-workspace or hostile-caller workload was run.
No generated answers were adjudicated for source support or citation correctness.
No timed write-then-recall workload was run.
No token or provider-cost accounting was performed.
Markdown is the documented canonical store; no corpus storage measurement was collected.

limits.text: This review inspected the README, PRD, observer, and reflector at the verified head; it did not inspect every rule, skill, scheduled job, or the separately installed semantic-search implementation.
The scripts require workspace/model configuration, local OpenCode, and scheduled invocation. No runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run; quality, timing, cost, and storage outcomes remain unknown.

The human review gate protects rule promotion in the current reflector, but the inspected system does not establish general correction auditing or complete deletion from version history and external copies.
